articles.title: Trump DOJ retreats by walking back affirmative action hiring lawsuit
articles.description: The Justice Department is invoking a landmark civil rights law as it walks back a lawsuit seeking to dismantle a state's affirmative action hiring policy. In a memorandum filed on Tuesday, the DOJ asked a three-judge panel for leave to amend its complaint in a lawsuit it first brought against the state on January 14. The suit accuses Minnesota of maintaining a "race- and sex-based affirmative action policy" for its state civil service that amounts to a "pattern or practice" violating Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the very statute written to bar discrimination in employment. The Civil Rights Division, led by Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon , says its rewritten complaint would sharpen the case into a purely "facial challenge" and seek only forward-looking relief. The rewritten complaint would instead seek a "declaratory judgment that Minnesota's affirmative action policy violates Title VII" and a "permanent injunction" barring the state from enforcing it, the DOJ wrote. DOJ lawyers cast the revision as an effort to streamline the fight and pointed to the court's instruction that the parties "work cooperatively throughout this litigation to narrow the issues in dispute." The DOJ insisted it had a "legitimate, good faith reason for bringing this Title VII lawsuit" and that it "in no way singled Minnesota out for enforcement action." The proposed complaint "lists various other active investigations to demonstrate that the United States is not selectively enforcing Title VII against Minnesota," the DOJ added. The new court filing complains that Minnesota's affirmative action rules "remained in effect following the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission's rescission of its affirmative action guidance," referring to guidance the government withdrew. The DOJ argued that the rewrite should cost the state nothing and told the court that its amended complaint is "likely to narrow (if not eliminate) the need for discovery" as the "case remains in its infancy."

articles.title: CNN reporter fires back at 'defensive' Mike Johnson over 'stupidest question'
articles.description: House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-LA) lashed out at CNN congressional correspondent Manu Raju on Tuesday after the reporter confronted him over his past predictions that the war in Iran would end quickly and cause only a temporary rise in gas prices. “You said repeatedly that this war was going to be over soon,” Raju told Johnson during a tense exchange on Capitol Hill. “You said that this would be a temporary blip — short-term — on gas prices. It has been more than six months. People are getting hurt still at the pump.” “Should the American people not also judge you on your projections?” Raju asked. “Your projections here have clearly been off base.” Johnson immediately snapped back. “Manu, that is one of the stupidest questions you’ve ever asked,” the speaker said. “I have nothing to do with the prosecution of the war across the globe.” While Raju quickly reminded Johnson that he has helped President Donald Trump sell his war with Iran to the American public, Johnson attempted to turn the question back on the CNN reporter. “So should the House speaker be held responsible for the duration of a military conflict around the globe?” Johnson asked, briefly patting Raju on the shoulder. “You should answer that question.” In a post on X after the brief back-and-forth, Raju described Johnson as “defensive” and added that “he snapped” after his questions. “Why is that stupid?” Raju fired back at Johnson. articles.title: Trump’s Lake Ontario name change clashes with a centuries-old treaty. Google Maps is on the hook, too
articles.description: According to the president of the Seneca Nation, President Donald Trump’s executive order to rename Lake Ontario to Lake America is more than merely controversial: It flies in the face of a 232-year-old treaty—and social media thinks mapping platforms like Google Maps are just as guilty. Last week, Trump signed the executive order, directing the Interior Department to change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America. It’s an apparent step in his ongoing trade fight with Canada. Earlier in August, the United States imposed 50% tariffs on hundreds of Canadian goods, which prompted Canada to do the same, with 50% tariffs on U.S. goods set to go into effect in September. Before signing the order, Trump posted on Truth Social that the U.S. was considering changing the name of the lake as “we don’t expect to be doing much business with Ontario any longer.” But what Trump saw as a dig toward Canada ignores the origins of the word Ontario, which far predate the name of any province, lake, or modern North American country. ‘Blatant disrespect’: How Trump’s order ignores history A day after Trump signed the order, the president of the Seneca Nation, J. Conrad Seneca, released a statement claiming that Trump’s move violates a treaty signed by George Washington in 1794. The Treaty of Canandaigua established, among other terms, “peace and friendship” between the U.S. and indigenous nations, including the Seneca Nation. It also noted that the Seneca Nation’s boundary begins “on Lake Ontario.” Seneca alleged that Trump’s order “violates that peace, friendship and commitments of the Canandaigua treaty,” reflecting “blatant disrespect toward the Seneca people.” “This is the latest in a long history of willful attempts to disregard the United States’ commitments to the Seneca and other Haudenosaunee nations,” he continued. “President Trump needs to be reminded of those commitments.” Seneca also pointed to the indigenous origins of the lake’s name. The word “Ontario” comes from the Wendat word “oniatarí:io,” which means “lake of shining waters.” In traditional Seneca language, the lake is called “sga:nyodai:yoh,” meaning “beautiful lake.” “The President cannot assert ownership over our culture or erase it through irresponsible political action. His order should be rescinded, and the name Lake Ontario should be left as it is, reflective of the Seneca people, other Haudenosaunee nations and all Indigenous people surrounding the lake,” Seneca said. “To us, Lake Ontario is not a political pawn,” he continued. “It does not separate the countries of the United States and Canada. It is all Indigenous land, which has been occupied by Indigenous people since time immemorial.” Seneca also highlighted that Article 6 of the Constitution refers to treaties as “the supreme Law of the Land.” Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also commented on Trump’s executive order, pointing out that Lake Ontario’s name “is more than 400 years old, predating both the Confederation of Canada and the Declaration of Independence of the United States of America.” “We know that America is changing. Their trading relationships, their foreign policies, their national monuments, their hydronyms,” Carney wrote in a post on X . “Canadians also know that naming reality means calling it Lake Ontario—then, now and always.” The name Lake Ontario comes from the Wendat word Ontari’io, which, appropriately, means “the lake is beautiful, the lake is big”. The name is more than 400 years old, predating both the Confederation of Canada and the Declaration of Independence of the United States of America.... — Mark Carney (@MarkJCarney) August 27, 2026 ‘Genuinely pathetic stuff’: Google catches the heat Google was the first major mapping platform to acquiesce to Trump’s order. Users in the U.S. will see the lake labeled as “Lake America,” while users in Canada will still see “Lake Ontario.” Users in other countries will see both names. Other leading map platforms, including Apple Maps and MapQuest, still show the lake as “Lake Ontario” on their maps. One viral post showed a screenshot from Google Maps showing the change to Lake America, calling the platform “so fucking embarrassing” and “genuinely pathetic stuff.” It’s garnered 4.9 million views. A response to that post , itself earning 1.3 million views, claimed that Google is “actively violating tribal rights with the Seneca Nation by doing this.” “Tech companies quietly accepting something so outrageously false makes me scared for when a government really goes hard with historical revisionism,” worried a third user . Google Maps is so fucking embarrassing man genuinely pathetic stuff pic.twitter.com/QuElL1Px2T — sam (@sam_d_1995) August 30, 2026 In response to Fast Company ’s request for comment, a representative for Google pointed to the company’s blog post on the change. The post explains that Google Maps reflects “official government sources,” which in the U.S. means the Geographic Names Information System. Since the GNIS changed the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America, Google followed suit. “These updates follow our long-standing policy for bodies of water with names that vary from country to country, and are starting to roll out now,” the post concludes. The backlash is similar to that faced by Google after Trump signed an executive order to rename the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America in 2025 . Then, too, Google followed Trump’s lead and changed the name of the gulf on its maps—though as a private mapping company, it’s not obligated to use the president’s preferred names, even if they’re made official by the GNIS.

articles.title: Trump Voters’ Confidence in Their Decision Dramatically Crumbles
articles.description: MANDEL NGAN / Mandel Ngan, Getty Images Donald Trump’s voters are becoming steadily less certain that they made the right call in returning him to the White House. Just 58 percent of Trump’s 2024 voters now say they are “very confident” they made the right choice, according to a new University of Massachusetts Amherst poll . That figure has fallen in four consecutive surveys, from 74 percent in April 2025 to 69 percent, then 62 percent and now 58 percent. But there is an important wrinkle. The proportion of Trump voters who say they would actually change their vote has not continued to climb. Read more at The Daily Beast.

Nobody should be forced to live under these conditions. Like D.C. and others, they will have almost no crime, FAST! The State and City can’t do what I do. Governor Pritzker, CALL!!! President DONALD J. TRUMP.” Trump has long been at war with Pritzker, a harsh critic who is considered a contender for the Democratic presidential nominee in 2008.

articles.title: IHC tells Adiala jail authorities to ensure Imran, Bushra Bibi are not kept in solitary confinement
articles.description: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Monday declared petitions challenging the alleged solitary confinement of PTI founder Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi maintainable and also directed Adiala jail authorities to ensure that neither was kept in solitary confinement. IHC’s Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro announced the verdict, which had been reserved on Aug 6, and held that the petitions were maintainable in light of the principles laid down in the Begum Nusrat Bhutto and Begum Shamim Afridi cases. The court also directed jail authorities to facilitate a meeting between Imran and Bushra in accordance with prison rules. It further ordered that Imran’s family members be allowed to meet him as permitted under the jail rules and directed authorities to make arrangements for telephone conversations between him and his sons. More to follow
